keyVerseText: And Adaiah the son of Jeroham, the son of Pashur, the son of Malchijah, and Maasiai the son of Adiel, the son of Jahzerah, the son of Meshullam, the son of Meshillemith, the son of Immer;
rootMeaning: The name אִמֵּר (ʼImmêr) derives from the Hebrew root אָמַר (ʼâmar), which broadly means 'to say' or 'to speak.' This root conveys not only the act of speaking but also implies declaration, command, and communication. The etymology 'talkative' suggests a person associated with speech or proclamation, adding a layer of meaning that the name may symbolize one who utters or declares God's word or commands, beyond simply serving as a proper name.
usageInScripture: The word אִמֵּר (ʼImmêr) consistently appears as a proper name in Scripture, referring primarily to individuals connected to the priestly lineage, including a priest in David's time and one in Jeremiah's era, as well as an ancestor of priests. Out of ten occurrences, it is mostly translated as 'of Immer' or 'and Immer,' indicating its function as a designation of family or tribal identity rather than a common noun. This consistent usage highlights its role as a marker of priestly heritage and continuity in the biblical narrative.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding אִמֵּר (ʼImmêr) as rooted in the concept of speech and declaration enriches our appreciation of the priestly role in Israel's worship and covenant relationship with God. Priests were not only mediators of sacrifice but also spokesmen for God's law and promises. The name's connection to 'he hath said' or 'talkative' underscores the importance of faithful proclamation and obedience to God's word, a theme central to the Christian faith. Christ, as the ultimate High Priest, perfectly embodies this role of divine speech and mediation, fulfilling what the priestly line symbolized in the Old Testament.
keyVerseReflection: In 1 Chronicles 9:12, Immer is mentioned as an ancestor within a detailed genealogical record: '...the son of Meshillemith, the son of Immer.' Here, the name functions as a vital link in the priestly lineage, affirming the continuity of God's appointed servants. The presence of Immer in this verse reminds readers that God's promises and commands have been faithfully transmitted through generations, a lineage ultimately fulfilled in Christ, the eternal priest who speaks and enacts God's word perfectly.
